checks.claim: Legal basis: 17 U.S.C. 105 makes copyright unavailable for works of the United States Government
checks.detail: Live copyright.gov text: 'Copyright protection under this title is not available for any work of the United States Government...'. Section 101 limits the term to a work prepared by an officer or employee as part of official duties.

checks.claim: Legal basis is clear for the whole TIGER product (the Census statement covers the files)
checks.detail: Section 105 covers Census-authored work. The TechDoc says the MAF/TIGER System is updated mainly by partner-supplied data from federal, state and local partners. State and local work is not a US Government work under section 101, and no statement found says what terms apply to partner-supplied features. The basis is clear for Census-authored content only. Not counsel-reviewed; this is not a legal opinion.

corrections: Names gap is far larger than stated. Statewide, 62.8% of 213613 vehicular TIGER features are unnamed (134137 records); the county range is 18.0% to 94.7% (median 61.7%). The 23 to 55 percent range covers only the three counties measured. Rural unlabelled lines will be most of the map unless names come from another source.

Statewide TIGER vehicular JSON, measured on all 56 counties: 168.95 MB before simplification, 77.07 MB at 2 m, 54.67 MB at 5 m. The recommendation's 69 MB (2 m) and 48 MB (5 m) are too low; use these values.

Dedupe rule must keep names. All 278 measured duplicate groups carry different FULLNAMEs; 'keep one record and carry its name if it has one' drops a name in each group. Dedupe saves only 1.3% to 1.8% of bytes statewide.

Attribution placement: the Census's requested statement belongs on the product's cover, the first page of the website, or elsewhere of comparable visibility. An About-page-only placement may not meet that.

Legal basis covers Census-authored content (17 U.S.C. 105). Partner-supplied features (state and local partners) are not addressed by that statute or by any statement found, so 'a clear, checked legal basis' should be qualified. Counsel review is still needed.
27th Street agreement is one-directional and the median is 6.77 m, not 6.28 m. State-file 27th Street vertices have 80.1% within 10 m of a TIGER 27th line and 11.4% with none within 50 m.
MSL abstract quote is not verbatim: the two sentences are not adjacent in the metadata; the quote omits the sentence between them without an ellipsis.
Minor re-fetch differences: the Census TIGER product page is 349,892 bytes (claimed 349,893) and the route-code page is 325,156 bytes (claimed 325,027); the quoted text is unchanged on both.
terms_check: All 17 quote entries in streets.json terms were checked against live text: the TechDoc PDF (sha256 matches the worker's), the Yellowstone ISO member, the state FGDC XML and _ReadMe.txt, the Census route-code page, and the Census Data API terms page. 16 are verbatim. 1 is not verbatim: the MSL abstract joins two non-adjacent sentences without an ellipsis. Phrase scans: 'public domain' occurs 0 times in the TIGER product page, the terms page, the TechDoc and the state metadata. Additional live pages scanned for reuse terms (Census policies index, MSL geoinfo home, MSDI page, transportation page, GIS data list): no license or reuse statement found. 17 U.S.C. 105 and the section 101 definition were read from the live copyright.gov text.
recommendation_note: The source choice stands: TIGER All Roads is the only candidate with a stated federal basis, and its counts, the Billings geometry agreement (median 0.91 m) and the statewide sizes reproduce from live data. It stands with corrections the owner must see before building: (1) statewide 62.8% of vehicular TIGER features are unnamed, not 23 to 55 percent, so most rural lines will be unlabelled; (2) statewide sizes are 168.95 / 77.07 / 54.67 MB (before / 2 m / 5 m), not 170 / 69 / 48; (3) the dedupe rule must keep names; (4) the attribution must sit on the first page or a comparably visible place; (5) the legal basis covers Census-authored content only and is not counsel-reviewed. If the owner needs names on most streets, the options are written reuse terms from the Montana State Library (names for 99.9% of records, status unknown) or a second named source, which the worker did not check (OpenStreetMap, MDT) and which would need its own terms review.
